events.title: SPARCstation 1 released
events.summary: [Sun] Microsystems began shipping the SPARCstation 1 in May 1989 — an affordable [RISC] [workstation] that brought [Unix] performance to technical desktops.
events.about: The SPARCstation line ran SunOS and Solaris with OpenWindows — [Java] was developed and launched on these machines. Developers built [client-server] apps, scientific simulations, and early web servers on SPARC before [x86] Linux commoditized servers. [Sun]'s NFS and RPC stack made networked [Unix] the default backend architecture.

narrative.whyChosen: The SPARCstation 1 made [RISC] [Unix] workstations affordable for mainstream technical computing.
narrative.whyImportant: It was the platform where [Java] and much of 1990s enterprise [Unix] software matured.
narrative.problemSolved: Engineers needed faster floating-point and graphics than Motorola 68000 [Sun]-1 boxes could deliver.
